[[File:Dodecahedron schlegel.svg|thumb|A map with twelve pentagonal faces]]
In [[topology]] and [[graph theory]], a '''map''' is a subdivision of a surface such as the [[Euclidean plane]] into [[Interior (topology)#Interior-disjoint shapes|interior-disjoint]] regions,
formed by [[graph embedding|embedding a graph]] onto the surface and forming connected components (faces) of the complement of the graph.
That is, it is a [[tessellation]] of the surface. A [[map graph]] is a graph derived from a map by creating a vertex for each face and an edge for each pair of faces that meet at a vertex or edge of the embedded graph.<ref>{{citation|first1=Jonathan|last1=Gross|first2=Jay|last2=Yellen|title=Graph Theory and its applications|year=1998|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=0-8493-3982-0|page=294}}</ref>
